name: English Civil Wars
what: Wars between Charles I and Parliament that ended with the king beheaded in 1649 and a republic.

name: French Wars of Religion
what: Eight civil wars between Catholic and Huguenot factions of the French nobility, ended by the Edict of Nantes.

name: The Fronde
what: Revolt of the Paris parlement and great nobles against the regency of Anne of Austria and Mazarin.

name: Wars of the Roses
what: Dynastic civil wars between the houses of Lancaster and York.

name: Hundred Years' War
what: Intermittent war between the English and French crowns for the French throne and lands.

name: Jacquerie
what: Peasant rising in the Beauvaisis and around Paris two years after the French king was captured at Poitiers.

name: English Rising of 1381 (Peasants' Revolt)
what: Rebels from Essex and Kent entered London demanding an end to serfdom after the third poll tax.

name: End of villeinage in England
what: Over the century after the Black Death, labour services and personal servitude faded out of English manors.

name: Second serfdom east of the Elbe
what: Lords in Poland, Prussia, Bohemia and Russia tied peasants to the land just as serfdom was dying in the west.

name: Celali revolts
what: Waves of rebellion by irregular musketeers and provincial governors that emptied much of rural Anatolia.

name: Yellow Turban Rebellion
what: Millenarian Daoist rising led by Zhang Jue; the generals raised to crush it became the warlords who carved up Han China.

name: An Lushan Rebellion
what: Revolt of the frontier general An Lushan that took both Tang capitals and left the provinces to military governors.

name: Taiping Rebellion
what: Civil war led by Hong Xiuquan's Heavenly Kingdom; among the deadliest wars of the nineteenth century.

name: Qing population boom
what: China's population roughly doubled to tripled under the high Qing, on new-world crops and frontier land.

name: Late Ming fiscal and silver crisis
what: Unpaid frontier armies, arrears in the land tax and a slump in silver imports hollowed out the Ming treasury.

name: Crisis of the Roman Republic
what: A century of land struggles, slave wars, the Social War and civil wars, from Tiberius Gracchus to Actium.

name: Reforms of Diocletian and Constantine
what: A larger army, a doubled number of provinces and a new tax system rebuilt the empire after the third-century crisis.

name: Huns push the Goths to the Danube
what: Tervingi and Greuthungi Goths fleeing the Huns asked to cross the Danube into the Roman Empire.

name: Material simplification of the post-Roman West
what: Coinage, wheel-made pottery, mortared building and long-distance trade vanished from much of the old western provinces, most of all Britain.

name: Collapse of Roman lead-silver mining
what: Greenland ice records European lead emissions falling after 165 CE and not recovering until about 750.

name: Third-century debasement of the silver coinage
what: The silver content of Roman coin fell below 4 percent before Aurelian reformed it in 274.

name: Polynesian settlement of Rapa Nui
what: Voyagers from East Polynesia reached the island; radiocarbon dating places it around 1200 CE.

name: Deforestation of Rapa Nui
what: The palm forest that covered the island disappeared within a few centuries of human arrival.

name: Rapa Nui rock gardens (lithic mulch)
what: Islanders mulched sweet-potato fields with broken stone to hold moisture and nutrients on a windy, poor soil.

name: Roggeveen reaches Rapa Nui
what: A Dutch expedition under Jacob Roggeveen landed on Easter Day 1722, the island's first recorded European contact.

name: Peruvian slave raids on Rapa Nui
what: Peruvian labour-recruiting ships carried off a large share of the islanders; returnees brought smallpox.

name: Rapa Nui population falls to 111
what: After raids, epidemics and emigration, 111 Rapanui were counted on the island in 1877.

name: Late Bronze Age megadrought (3.2 ka event)
what: Pollen and lake cores from Cyprus, Syria and the Sea of Galilee show a drier eastern Mediterranean for about 150 years.

name: Ramesses III fights the Sea Peoples
what: Medinet Habu reliefs record the year-8 land and sea battles against a coalition of migrants and raiders.

name: Late Bronze Age earthquake storm
what: A cluster of earthquakes along the Aegean and Levantine faults, proposed to explain destruction layers at Mycenae, Troy and Ugarit.

name: Greek Dark Age
what: After the palaces fell, Greece lost writing, monumental building and most of its settlements for three centuries.

name: 4.2 ka drought event
what: A centuries-long dry spell recorded from the Mediterranean to the Indus.

name: Late Classic Maya endemic warfare
what: Kingdoms of the Petexbatun and beyond fortified their cities and fought until royal courts were abandoned.

name: Khmer court leaves Angkor for the Mekong
what: After Ayutthaya took Angkor, the Khmer court moved south to the Phnom Penh region and its river trade.

name: Decline and abandonment of Cahokia
what: The largest Mississippian town shrank through the 1200s and was empty by about 1350.

name: Glorious Revolution
what: William of Orange displaced James II; the Bill of Rights put taxation and the army under Parliament.

name: English financial revolution
what: A funded national debt and the Bank of England (1694) let the crown borrow cheaply and at scale.

name: British Industrial Revolution
what: Coal, steam and factory textiles started sustained growth of output per head in Britain.

name: Toledo's mining mita at Potosí
what: Viceroy Francisco de Toledo forced one in seven adult men of a fixed catchment to work the Potosí and Huancavelica mines.

name: Lasting poverty of former mita districts
what: Two centuries after abolition, households inside the old mita boundary consume about a quarter less than those just outside.

name: Division of Korea
what: Soviet and American occupation zones along the 38th parallel became two states with opposite economic systems.

name: North and South Korean incomes diverge
what: From similar starting points, South Korea became a high-income economy while North Korea stagnated and starved.

name: Serrata of the Venetian Great Council
what: The Great Council was closed to families not already in it, turning an open merchant elite into a hereditary nobility.

name: Golden age of labour after the Black Death
what: With a third or more of workers dead, real wages in much of Europe and the Middle East roughly doubled.

name: Second World War
what: The deadliest war in history, fought with total mobilisation of economies across Eurasia and America.

name: The Great Compression
what: Wage and income gaps in the United States and much of the West narrowed sharply in the 1940s and stayed narrow for decades.

name: New Deal
what: Federal relief, labour law, social security and progressive taxation under Franklin Roosevelt.

name: Communist land reform in China
what: Landlord land was seized and redistributed by village struggle meetings, many ending in executions.

name: Genocide against the Tutsi in Rwanda
what: Over about a hundred days, Hutu Power militias and soldiers killed most of the Tutsi of Rwanda and Hutu who opposed them.

name: Rural Rwanda land pressure
what: One of the densest farming populations in Africa, with farms subdivided below subsistence size.

name: Tokugawa forest regulation
what: After a seventeenth-century timber crisis, shogunate and domains restricted cutting and planted forests.

name: Mughal jagirdari crisis
what: Too many nobles chased too few revenue assignments, squeezing peasants and setting nobles against each other.

name: Rise of the Mughal successor states
what: Governors in Awadh, Bengal and Hyderabad made themselves hereditary rulers under nominal Mughal sovereignty.

name: Teotihuacan builds apartment compounds
what: After about 250 CE the city stopped building pyramids and housed most of its people in roomy stone apartment compounds.

name: North Korean collective farming and planning
what: State farms, central food distribution and self-reliance doctrine under Kim Il Sung.

name: Warlord era in China
what: After Yuan Shikai's death, rival military cliques ruled China's provinces; Olson took the warlord Feng Yuxiang as his stationary bandit.
